blocks.text: King Edward Village — Knight Street / Kingsway / East King Edward Avenue (Aquilini Group)

King Edward Village by Aquilini Group: 398 homes over shops on the ground and part of the second floor, in concrete buildings of 5, 7, 12 and 17 storeys, freehold strata, zoned CD-1. It was built in phases; listings give 2007 (4078 Knight Street) and 2008 (4028 Knight Street), and the shopping podium 2009, so check the strata plan for a specific building. The podium has a Save-On-Foods, a Vancouver Public Library branch and services. A 4078 Knight Street listing calls the building "Rental Friendly (Nothing Less than 30 days)", which fits the rules: long-term rental bans are void, but stays under 30 days can still be limited.
Streets, schools and getting around Knight

items.t: "Knight" is the Knight Street corridor in Vancouver East: the major north–south arterial running from the Clark Drive / Great Northern Way area south through Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview to the Knight Street Bridge over the Fraser River's north arm to Richmond. The City lists "Knight" as a recognised smaller area, but it is not one of the City's 22 distinct local areas.

Where the condos are: mostly in one place, Kingsway and King Edward Avenue at Knight Street, where King Edward Village has the area's apartment condos above its shops. Elsewhere there are detached houses on the side streets, newer townhouses (Knight 18, The Charles) on and just off Knight, and commercial and mixed-use buildings on Knight Street itself.
Cross streets that structure the corridor: East Broadway, Kingsway, East 33rd Avenue, East 41st Avenue, East 49th Avenue and SE Marine Drive.
Transit: the corridor is crossed by the R4 41st Ave RapidBus and the 41 at East 41st Avenue, the 49 at East 49th Avenue, and the 9 at East Broadway; no SkyTrain station sits on the corridor.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Knight

items.t: Area plans: the Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview / Killarney community visions apply to the local areas the corridor runs through, alongside the citywide Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026. The June 2025 Conwest referral also records that Council repealed the Kensington-Cedar Cottage Community Vision in November 2023 — the old vision is no longer current policy for the King Edward node.

The grocery store, library and bank are inside the condo development. King Edward Village's podium holds the Save-On-Foods, the Vancouver Public Library branch and services that listings describe as "right at your door step" — the amenity is the podium tenancy mix (the retail podium is 92.20% occupied in the brokerage source, with Save-On-Foods, TD, Service Canada and the library occupying 71.81% of it), so a change in podium tenancies changes daily life in the towers above.

Council's 2007 neighbourhood-centres report records the Knight and Kingsway plan adding capacity for about 800 further ground-oriented homes on top of the over-370 units on the King Edward Village site; the 2025 Conwest referral records that the Kensington-Cedar Cottage Community Vision that framed the node was repealed in November 2023. Policy citations for this corner need a date check.

The health centre is on the street itself. South Community Health Centre, 6405 Knight Street at East 49th Avenue, provides public and community health services for South Vancouver from an address on the corridor — one of the few civic anchors physically on Knight Street.

Knight 18's name and its phase count do not match — check the disclosure. The current 3430 Knight Street listing names the project "Knight 18" while recording 7 units in the development phase shown and a 2026 build year; a buyer needs the disclosure statement / strata plan to reconcile the full collection size before relying on either figure.

A current listing says pets are allowed; confirm on the Form B. Presale marketing expected completion between spring 2024 and summer 2025, but listings show 2026, so completion dates here slipped, which matters for any homes still sold by the developer.

items.t: Where the townhouses are: at the north end, in Kensington-Cedar Cottage. Knight 18 is at Knight Street and East 18th Avenue and The Charles is at East 21st Avenue and Knight Street, both just off the Kingsway business district.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Knight

items.t: For Knight 18 (and The Charles, if it turns out to be strata), read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. For a 2026 complex, the Form B also shows which phase's strata a unit is in, which sorts out Knight 18's name, phases and unit count. Rental and pet lines in listings aren't the bylaws.

Fee-simple homes on the side streets: most duplexes and multiplexes here are fee simple. If The Charles turns out to be fee simple rather than strata, these rules apply to it instead, which is why its ownership type matters.

Side-street house lots: detached houses on the side streets east and west of the arterial, with commercial, mixed-use and strata product on the Knight Street frontage itself and at the avenue crossings. A fee-simple lot carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees. Frontage position is the defining pricing fact: Knight Street frontage lots carry arterial exposure (truck traffic, noise) and price differently from side-street houses one block in — never comp one against the other without an explicit frontage adjustment.

Lot character: the residential side streets sit under the R1-1 District Schedule of Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 — minimum site area 306 m² for a single detached house or duplex and for a multiple dwelling of 3 to 4 units (minimum frontage 10.0 m), 464 m² for 5 units (13.4 m), 557 m² for 6 to 8 units (15.1 m); a single detached house may include a secondary suite and a laneway house, and a multiplex may have up to 6 units or up to 8 rental units.
Serviced position: corridor homes are on City water and sewer services.

Flood position: the corridor's south end descends to the Fraser River's north arm at the Knight Street Bridge and the City's designated floodplain includes the coastal floodplain along the Fraser River in South Vancouver; parcels in it carry Vancouver Building By-law setback and flood construction level requirements.

King Edward Village, at Knight Street, Kingsway and East King Edward Avenue, by Aquilini Group: one planned mixed-use development, with homes at 4028 and 4078 Knight Street, 1432 Kingsway and 1483 East King Edward Avenue. It has 398 homes over shops on the ground and part of the second floor, in concrete buildings of 5, 7, 12 and 17 storeys, freehold strata, zoned CD-1. It was built in phases, and sources give 2007, 2008 and 2009.

Conwest proposal, 4001–4009 Knight Street and 1348 East 24th Avenue: a rezoning application that City staff recommend refusing. It would rezone from C-2 and RM-1 to CD-1 for a 23-storey mixed-use building with 233 strata homes, a 37-space childcare facility and ground-floor shops. City staff's June 3, 2025 report recommends that the application be refused following the public hearing. Nothing is built or for sale, so don't count on these 233 homes.

BC Housing supportive housing — 1406 and 1410 East King Edward Avenue. Proposed non-market housing, excluded: A proposed social / supportive housing building at Knight Street and East King Edward Avenue (12 storeys and approximately 90 studio homes with supports in the BC Housing fact sheet; a later application report describes a 14-storey building with 109 modular studio units) for adults, seniors and people with disabilities experiencing or at risk of homelessness, to be operated by non-profit housing societies. Non-market housing — not strata lots or homes for sale in any form.

items.t: Nearby areas: Fraser VE along Fraser Street to the west, Killarney and Champlain Heights to the east, Mount Pleasant and Riley Park to the north-west, and Richmond across the Knight Street Bridge to the south.

Civic anchors near the corridor: Memorial South Park, 5955 Ross Street, in Sunset west of the corridor; Sunset Community Centre on Main Street near East 49th Avenue and Killarney Community Centre, 6260 Killarney Street, are the nearest Park Board centres named. The South Hill Branch library, on Fraser Street west of the corridor, serves the west side.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Knight

items.t: Plans — local-area visions (one repealed) + Vancouver Official Development Plan: the Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview / Killarney community visions apply to the local areas the corridor runs through, alongside the citywide Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026. Date-check any policy citation for the King Edward node: the June 2025 Conwest referral records that Council repealed the Kensington-Cedar Cottage Community Vision in November 2023 — the old vision is no longer current policy for that corner.

Strata rules (for King Edward Village, Knight 18 and any bare-land strata lot): check the Form B (fees, amounts owing, levies, contingency reserve balance and insurance; within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page). At King Edward Village, the depreciation report also shows costs tied to the podium, parkade and shops. Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, and at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve. Rental bans are void, but short-term rentals can still be limited, as in King Edward Village's "nothing less than 30 days" rule. Only 55+ age bylaws are valid, and none of the complexes here is 55+. For The Charles, check the ownership type first: if it's fee simple, there's no Form B, just the title and City rules.

items.t: The grocery store, library and bank are inside the condo development: King Edward Village's podium holds the Save-On-Foods, the Vancouver Public Library branch and services listings describe as "right at your door step" — the retail podium is 92.20% occupied in the brokerage source, with Save-On-Foods, TD, Service Canada and the library occupying 71.81% of it — so a change in podium tenancies changes daily life on the site above it.

Knight 18's name and numbers don't match: it's named for its corner at Knight Street and 18th Avenue, current listings show 7 units, and older presale marketing said 12. Only the disclosure statement gives the full count.

The newest townhouses here arrived about two years late: The Charles' presale marketing expected completion in summer 2023 or fall 2024, but the first resale shows 2025, the same pattern as Knight 18 (expected spring 2024, built 2026). Allow for delays on presale completion dates here.

The corridor's south end is a bridge, not a boundary street: Knight Street carries Highway 99 traffic over the Knight Street Bridge to Richmond — for north-end owners that is the Richmond/YVR route from the front door, and for side-street owners it is the source of the truck traffic priced as frontage exposure.

faq.a: At one node: King Edward Village at Knight Street, Kingsway and East King Edward Avenue — 398 residences in buildings of 5, 7, 12 and 17 storeys over a retail podium. The rest of the corridor is side-street houses and townhouse infill.
faq.q: Where are the Knight corridor's condos, actually?

faq.a: They are addresses within the one King Edward Village development by the Aquilini Group — listings under all four addresses carry the King Edward Village name. Price and compare them as one development's phases/faces, not as four competing buildings.
faq.q: Are 4028 Knight, 4078 Knight, 1432 Kingsway and 1483 King Edward different buildings?

faq.a: Sources conflict — 2007 in a 4078 Knight Street listing, 2008 in 4028 Knight Street listings, 2009 for the retail podium in the brokerage source — consistent with phased completion.
faq.q: What year was King Edward Village built?

faq.a: Long-term, yes — rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022, and the building is marketed as rental friendly with a nothing-less-than-30-days term, which is the enforceable short-term restriction. Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax declaration still applies if the unit sits empty.
faq.q: Can I rent out a King Edward Village condo?

faq.a: Read the registered bylaws in the strata package before writing. Pet bylaws remain enforceable in BC.
faq.q: Are pets allowed at King Edward Village?

faq.a: The name says 18; current listings record 7 units in the development as sold/marketed and the presale source describes 7 family-size townhomes in two 3-storey woodframe buildings; an older presale archive records 12 units. The disclosure statement and strata plan settle it — treat none of the three figures as the project total without them.
faq.q: Knight 18 — is it 7 homes, 12 homes, or 18?

faq.a: It matters: strata means a Form B, a depreciation report and a reserve fund; fee simple means none of those, just the title and City rules. Get the disclosure statement or a title search before making an offer.
faq.q: Is The Charles strata or fee-simple?

faq.a: Only if that side is legally separate — a strata lot in a 2-lot strata plan, or its own fee-simple lot from a subdivision. Check the title first.
faq.q: Can I buy just one side of a duplex on the Knight corridor?

faq.a: Fee simple by default: no strata, Form B or strata fees; check the title, the R1-1 zoning and any registered covenants. Strata rules apply only where the title shows a strata lot.
faq.q: Is a side-street duplex here strata or fee-simple?

faq.a: Not one of the 22 distinct local areas — the City lists "Knight" as a recognised smaller area; the Knight Street corridor runs through the Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview local areas.
faq.q: Is "Knight" an official City of Vancouver neighbourhood?

faq.a: The Knight Street Bridge over the Fraser River's north arm to Richmond — the City frames Victoria-Fraserview as lying between the Knight Street Bridge and Killarney.
